messages:
maya: Quick thread — followup on the rollout schema stuff. I sketched a small proposal: split "intent" (what the rollout is trying to achieve) from "anchor/lease" (the actual pinned model id). Intent can be canary/ramp/hotfix/emergency and should carry duration + metric targets. Soft-anchors TTLs only enforced server-side. Sketch below.

oz: +1 on separation. One question: how do we express fallback order and compatibility tokens? Clients sometimes need a hint to degrade gracefully.

maya: thinking: include optional "compatibility_token" (opaque string) and "fallback_priority" (ordered list of model ids). If token mismatches, clients can opt into a "degrade" mode. Default: server-side enforcement, expose only hints to clients.

kevin: We also need observability hooks: attach "probe_set_id" and "expected_metric" in rollout metadata so Console and SRE can auto-wire evaluations. Otherwise someone has to manually map rollouts -> evals.

anya: ops note: add an "abort_window" (seconds) so we can define an automatic abort window after rollout where violations trigger auto-abort. 0 = disabled.

release-bot: deploy 1768123456 started by maya. status: staging. :rocket:

maya: example metadata snippet (informal):
```json
{
  "intent": "canary",
  "ttl": "3600",
  "compatibility_token": "v3-llm-a",
  "fallback_priority": ["v2-llm-a", "v1-llm-a"],
  "probe_set": "latency-qa-27",
  "abort_window": 300
}
```
(note: on the wire we keep everything as strings for simplicity in older clients)

oz: clarify TTL semantics: does TTL mean "soft unbind after ttl" (intent expires) or "auto-evict from pool"? I think we want soft unbind: anchor remains until explicit eviction.

maya: correct — TTL is a soft expiration for the intent only, not a hard deletion. We'll add an optional "anchor_state": "soft" | "hard" to indicate stronger semantics when needed.

kevin: suggestion: include "reason" free text and a small enum "reason_category" (perf/regression/security) for easy filtering in Console.

anya: ops concern: ensure private deployments don't leak probe_set ids out of the customer control plane. Make probe_set an opaque id resolved by the control plane only.

oz: compatibility/migration question: how do we roll out the new "fallback_priority" field? Backcompat: keep it optional; old clients treat unknown fields as hints. Server will provide a compatibility_shim for very old resolvers.

maya: agreed. also propose adding "rollout_group" (opaque grouping id) so Console can group related rollouts, e.g. "payment-llm-aug2026".

kevin: tiny add: "observability_level": "none|minimal|full" so we can gate how much telemetry to attach per rollout (useful for PII-sensitive customers).

anya: LGTM. Can someone put this into an RFC PR with diagrams + migration plan? I'll help write the diagrams and list the edgecases.

maya: I will open the PR today with the schema, examples, and a migration checklist. tagging @oz @kevin @anya for review.

oz: ack, will review after lunch.

kevin: ack. thanks maya.

release-bot: deploy 1768123456 moved to canary by maya. metrics pipeline: probe_set=latency-qa-27.
